scope: Private archive materialization, exact existing reuse, bounded static capture-directory exclusion, directory ownership, durability, cancellation checkpoints and retained partials. Producer authority/HTTP and registered-task lifetime are separate Root/E reviews.

preservedFindings.finding: Only lexical capture exclusion allowed a distinct non-symlink physical alias into the capture.
preservedFindings.currentCorrection: The retained capture descriptor supplies a bounded no-follow directory-identity census; output parents and every examined real ancestor must be outside that identity set.

preservedFindings.finding: EEXIST readback did not establish file or directory durability after a previous failed sync.
preservedFindings.currentCorrection: Both paths independently verify the same read descriptor, require file and retained-parent fsync, then recheck descriptor/named/parent identities.

preservedFindings.finding: A disjoint journal parent did not exclude static capture aliases at the actual AnyDestinationMigrationV1/binding-scope descendants.
preservedFindings.currentCorrection: The actual plan binding derives the identical original Journal scope; the two existing directories are opened, excluded from capture identities and retained. Prospective directories are reopened and checked once present under the stable private-namespace owner.

preservedFindings.finding: Both temporary dup calls dropped close-on-exec.

checks: All eight current storage literal changes and the single producer binding change apply and reverse to complete predecessor bytes exactly.
The earlier three producer storage-scope changes apply and reverse exactly to E-reviewed b79eda7132645e4e91d3da2877e63a64469dfb40.
The original Journal account/Space/store/plan hash material and AnyDestinationMigrationV1 directory name match exactly; Journal and Executor source remain unchanged.

Capture census opens no file contents; it refuses nonregular/nondirectory entries, repeated directory identities and invalid names, with at most 100000 entries, at most 10000 admitted directories, depth at most 32 and a 256-step output ancestry bound.
Private base directories are current-owner 0700, checked by descriptor and pathname; opened scope ownership transfers only after admission and failures close acquired descriptors.
Fresh archive creation uses descriptor-relative EXCL/NOFOLLOW/CLOEXEC, current-owner regular nlink1 0600 then 0400, exact size and stable named identity.
Archive name uses an independently recomputed SHA256; contents are 4096 through 64 MiB, and independent readback reads at most expected bytes plus one before rejecting an oversize result.
Existing output must be exact current-owner 0400 regular nlink1 bytes/hash; it is never rewritten or chmodded.
Cancellation is checked before output work, while walking metadata, during readback and at final scope validation. Failed/partial output is not removed or automatically replaced.
Storage is captured through the producer authorization closure and checked before/after destination validation and final producer return.
lifetimeAndNamespaceLimits: The real private App namespace owner must serialize directory moves, mounts and removal through the entire outer registered-operation drain; source checks do not implement an OS namespace lock.

Base directory descriptors and initially present journal-child descriptors are retained through produce's storage I/O. Previously absent children are reopened and checked by validate; this is not a claim that their first observed descriptor is retained permanently.
The unchanged Journal still receives a URL and creates/opens its own plan-directory descriptor. The new scope is not descriptor injection into Journal.

Storage descriptor lifetime may end after produce returns; the outer lease/delivery-only await performs no further storage I/O, while App namespace ownership must continue through that await and drain.
No atomic protection against an independent administrator rename/mount, no global filesystem mutation audit and no actual platform/crash durability qualification are claimed.
Ordinary cancellation cannot abort an arbitrary blocking filesystem syscall. Cleanup retains owned partials and waits for the enclosing owned task, as separately reviewed.

tests.fourAdditionalStorageControls: Not included in this peer; their focused source review is separate.

sourceReviewPreparationCorrection.correction: The directory count guard checks count < 10000 before inserting, so the admitted maximum is 10000. Only this reporting wording was corrected before handoff; no source or runtime change.
